requirements.text: I need it set to moderate priority and handled by Anne Medina
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 10 AND priority = 'moderate' AND assigned_to = 29 AND assignment_group = 4 AND status = 'draft'
assumptions: case HRC0000720 is hr_case 10; its number is fixed by the anchor
'currently in planning' is the case's seed priority, planning; moderate is the new priority
Anne Medina is user 29, the only user of that name

assignment_group 4 (HR Service Desk) implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assignee to be an active member of the case's group, Anne Medina is not in the current group 5, and the request adds her to group 4
status draft kept from the benchmark check; the request asks for no status change and the case is draft on the seed

requirements.text: Update the case description for Marc Henry accordingly

assumptions: the case has no description column; short_description is its description
the case is opened for HR profile 20, Marc Henry
the three terms kept from the benchmark check; 'accordingly' ties the text to the onboarding case, its subject and the new skill

id assumed next in sequence (highest skill_id on the seed is 19)
name 'Visa Compliance' without the word Skill, as every seed skill is named; kept from the benchmark check
active true kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
org_id 1 kept from the benchmark check; the acting user and every existing skill are in org 1

requirements.text: create a Moderate Onboarding Visa Routing assignment rule that directs moderate priority cases requiring this new skill to that same group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignment_rules WHERE assignment_rule_id = 9 AND name = 'Moderate Onboarding Visa Routing' AND based_on_priority = 'moderate' AND based_on_skills LIKE '%Visa Compliance%' AND user_group = 4 AND active = true AND org_id = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest assignment_rule_id on the seed is 8)
'that same group' is HR Service Desk, group 4
based_on_skills added: the rule routes cases requiring the new skill, and every seed rule stores its skills as a JSON list of skill names, so the name must appear in it
active true kept from the benchmark check; a rule meant to route future cases must be active
org_id 1 kept from the benchmark check; every existing rule and the group are in org 1
based_on_country not fixed by request or policy, so not tested

requirements.text: ensure the draft notification for this case is ready for the next outgoing batch
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 10 AND hr_case_id = 10 AND email = 'marc.henry.20@personal.example.com' AND type = 'report' AND status = 'ready' AND org_id = 10
assumptions: notification 10 is the only notification for case 10 and is draft on the seed
'ready for the next outgoing batch' read as status ready, a status other notifications hold on the seed
hr_case_id, email, type and org_id are the row's seed values, kept from the benchmark check; the request does not change them

notes:
The two passes agree on every row, id, cell and disposition (all seven checks kept); their assumptions differ in wording only. One carried the case's priority and assignee and its description in one requirement, the other in two; the request asks for them in separate sentences, so they are two requirements here, and both carry the benchmark's case check and the combined check.
The case check's number predicate is dropped because the anchor hr_case_id 10 names the same row. The combined check is a conjunction of the six other checks and is carried jointly by every requirement. The acting user, Joanne Simpson, holds the manager role; the policy says managers cannot modify system configuration and lists assignment rules among the administrator's tables, so creating the skill and the rule could be refused under a strict reading. The file follows the request and the benchmark, which both expect every step done; a strict reading would turn the skill and assignment-rule requirements into stays. The case's skills column (JSON) is null on every seed case, so its storage format is not shown and no cell is written for it, although the request implies the case needs the Visa Compliance skill. The policy's short-description format (Service, Subject, Detail) and its 30-120 character limit are not tested by the benchmark and are left out. The case and its notification belong to org 10, while Anne Medina, HR Service Desk, the skill and the rule are in org 1; the benchmark's checks accept this and so do these requirements. No stay requirement: the request forbids nothing and selects no set of rows by description.
